assurance.text: AI with zero data retention (ZDR): enforced on every request
assurance.title: Every AI call enforces zdr=true and data_collection=deny at OpenRouter.

todo.label: To handle
todo.empty: Nothing to handle. Fetch your mailboxes, or connect one in Mailboxes.

none.label: No reply needed
none.empty: No email set aside by triage.

sent.label: Replied
sent.empty: No reply sent or saved as a draft yet.

auth.askInvitation: No account? Ask your administrator for an invitation.
auth.firstAccount: No account exists yet. Create your organisation: you will be its administrator.
auth.organizationHint: Your company or team. You will be its administrator and can invite others.
auth.name: Your name
auth.nameHint: Shown to the other members in place of your address. Optional.
auth.pointEuTitle: Compliant with the GDPR and the EU AI Act.
auth.pointEu: Your data does not leave servers in Europe.
auth.pointZdr: Zero data retention, enforced on every AI request.
auth.pointMinimal: The AI is sent as little as possible.

invitation.invited: You have been invited to join {organization} on {product}.
invitation.title: Join your team

mailbox.fetched: {count, plural, =0 {No new email.} one {# email fetched.} other {# emails fetched.}}

reading.pendingTriage: Not sorted yet: it will be at the next fetch.

reply.draftNotice: This message has not been sent: it is waiting in the Drafts folder of your mailbox, where you can finish and send it.

composer.title: Your reply
composer.reasonPlaceholder: E.g. too formal, I am on first-name terms with this client
composer.reasonHint: Optional. Your next proposals with this prompt take it into account; the administrators can read it to improve the prompt.
composer.saveDraftTitle: Files the reply in the Drafts folder of your mailbox, without sending it
composer.noKey: No OpenRouter key configured: add one in <link>Settings</link> to get proposals.
composer.noPrompt: No prompt available: ask an administrator to create one.
composer.placeholder: Write your reply, or just a few notes on what to say.
composer.typosTitle: Corrects spelling and grammar, and changes nothing else. The email received is not sent to the AI.
composer.styleTitle: Rewrites for clarity and tone, keeping the meaning. The email received is not sent to the AI.
composer.applyPromptTitle: Writes the reply from the email received and from what you wrote, in the way this prompt describes.
composer.confirmSendText: It leaves from your mailbox right away and cannot be taken back.
composer.helpNote: Typos and style work on your text only: the email received is not sent to the AI.
composer.toComplete: {count, plural, one {# passage in square brackets is still to complete.} other {# passages in square brackets are still to complete.}}
composer.closedNone: No reply is expected: the reply area stays closed until you ask for it.
composer.closedIgnored: This email is ignored: the reply area stays closed until you ask for it.

prompts.title: Prompts
prompts.intro: Each prompt describes a way of replying. They belong to the organisation: at triage the AI may suggest the most suitable one, and every member remains free to choose another for each email. Members see the name and the description, not the instructions.
prompts.name: Name
prompts.whenHint: The AI reads this description to suggest the right prompt for each email.
prompts.instructionsHint: Tone, structure, business rules. The common instructions (language of the email, plain text, invent nothing, signature) are added automatically.
prompts.correctionsHint: What members changed in this prompt’s proposals, and why. Each one only applies to its author’s proposals: fold into the instructions those that hold for everyone.
prompts.usage: {used, plural, one {# reply} other {# replies}}, {edited, plural, =0 {none edited} other {# edited}}
prompts.templatesHint: Other ways of replying, ready to add. Once added they are yours to edit.

users.title: Users
users.intro: Members of {organization}. Administrators manage the prompts, the invitations, the shared mailboxes and the organisation's settings. They have no access to a member's personal mailbox.
users.linkReady: Invitation link for {email} — valid for {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}, usable once. Pass it on yourself: it will not be shown again.
users.copyFailed: Could not copy: select the link and copy it.
users.confirmDelete: Delete the account {email}? Its connected mailboxes, emails and replies stored here will be erased. The mailbox itself is not touched.

accounts.title: Mailboxes
accounts.confirmDisconnect: Disconnect {email}? The emails and replies stored here will be deleted (your mailbox is not touched).
accounts.oauthIntro: No password is entered here: you grant access at Google or Microsoft (reading the inbox, drafts and sending).
accounts.oauthUnavailable: Not available: sign-in with this provider is not set up on this server ({prefix}_CLIENT_ID / _SECRET variables).
accounts.name: Name
accounts.tlsHint: Direct TLS: ports 993 (IMAP) and 465 (SMTP). Unchecked, the connection uses STARTTLS (143 / 587).
accounts.connected: Mailbox connected. Now choose the folder to watch.
accounts.chooseFolder: These are the folders of your own mailbox, as your mail provider lists them. Only the emails of the one you choose are fetched.
accounts.folderPending: An administrator has yet to choose the folder to watch.
accounts.intro: Each mailbox watches one folder. A shared mailbox is used by every member; only administrators connect, change or disconnect one.
accounts.step3: Try it on a first email
accounts.connectIntro: The emails of one folder that you choose are fetched, and your replies are sent from the same address. Nothing else in the mailbox is read.
accounts.mineHint: A personal mailbox. Only you see its emails; administrators have no access to it.
accounts.sharedHint: contact@, info@… Every member of {organization} sees its emails and can reply from it.
accounts.imapHint: With its address and a password (IMAP / SMTP).
accounts.passwordHint: The password is encrypted in the database. Prefer an application password.
accounts.connectHint: The connection is tested before anything is saved.
accounts.keyIntro: Sorting your emails and writing proposals go through OpenRouter, with your organisation’s own key. Without one you can still read and answer by hand.
accounts.keyHint: Create one in your <link>OpenRouter account</link>. It is encrypted in the database and used by every member who has no key of their own.
accounts.serversProposed: Filled in from the address. Check them with your mail provider if the connection fails.
accounts.hostedSignIn: {address} is hosted at {provider}: connect it by signing in there, no password is typed here.
accounts.hostedPassword: {address} is hosted at {provider}, which usually refuses the mailbox’s own password. Use an application password, or ask whoever hosts this server to set up sign-in with {provider}.

settings.title: Settings
settings.noKey: No OpenRouter key: automatic triage and proposals are disabled.
settings.modelHint: Identifier “provider/model”. Leave empty for your organisation's model ({model}). The model must have at least one ZDR provider, otherwise the request is refused.
settings.signatureHint: Added as is at the end of each proposal.
settings.keyHint: Encrypted in the database. Leave empty to use your organisation's key.
settings.keyHintOwn: Leave empty to keep the current key.
settings.privacyPolicy: Every request sent to OpenRouter carries {policy}. This cannot be disabled.
settings.privacyLogging: In your OpenRouter account, keep prompt logging disabled (Settings → Privacy): that setting belongs to your account, not to this application.
settings.privacyRetention: Email content is erased from this application after {days, plural, one {# day} other {# days}}.
settings.privacyNoRetention: Email content is kept without limit in this application.
settings.privacyEncryption: Passwords, OAuth tokens and API keys are encrypted in the database (AES-256-GCM).
settings.privacyValidation: No email is sent without your explicit validation.
settings.privacyReasons: The reasons you give when editing a proposal are visible to your organisation's administrators, who use them to improve the prompts. The emails of your personal mailbox are not.
settings.appearanceText: Colours, typography, logo and name come from the server's brand folder. <link>See the style guide</link> to check how every component renders.
settings.privacyTriageNone: Fetched emails are not analysed by the AI: every email of the folder you watch is to be handled, apart from plainly automated mail (newsletters, notifications), which local rules set aside. Email content only goes to the AI when you ask for a proposal.
settings.privacyTriageAi: Fetched emails are sorted by the AI, which reads their sender, subject, the beginning of their text and the names of their attachments. Plainly automated mail (newsletters, notifications) is set aside by local rules first and never sent to it.
settings.name: Your name
settings.nameHint: Shown to the other members of {organization}, in place of your address.
settings.privacyIntro: What {product} guarantees about your email. None of it can be switched off.

guarantee.minimal: The AI sees as little as possible

settings.privacyZdr: Every AI request requires a provider that keeps nothing and trains on nothing. If none can guarantee it, the request fails instead of being routed elsewhere.
settings.privacyPrepared: A proposal is prepared at fetch for each email to handle: its content is then sent to the AI without anyone asking.

styleguide.title: Style guide — {product}
styleguide.intro: Every token and component of the design system, rendered with this installation's brand. Edit theme.css in the brand folder, then reload this page to judge the result.
styleguide.brandInputsHint: Defined in brand/theme.css. Everything else follows from them.
styleguide.colorsHint: What components are allowed to use. Computed from the brand, in light and dark mode alike.
styleguide.heading: Level {level} heading
styleguide.paragraph: Body paragraph, with strong text, code and a link.
styleguide.cardText: A card groups one subject: a title, optional badges, a content.
styleguide.emails: Email row, message body, empty state
styleguide.shellNote: The frame of the application (side navigation) is the AppShell organism: it is seen in the application itself.

Hello,

Body of a message in plain text, as it was received.

Kind regards

  • a first point
  • a second one

See the documentation.

A quoted line.

styleguide.iconsHint: Lucide, self-hosted. An icon never stands alone without a label or an accessible name.
styleguide.dialogText: It will leave from your mailbox right away.
styleguide.dialogDangerText: The replies already written with it are kept.
styleguide.aiNote: Written by the AI with a prompt. Read it before you send.

organization.title: Organisation
organization.intro: These settings apply to every member and every mailbox of the organisation.
organization.name: Name
organization.triageNone: None: every email of the watched folder is to be handled
organization.triageAi: By the AI: it decides whether a reply is needed and suggests a prompt
organization.triageHint: Sorting by the AI costs one request per 20 emails fetched, and sends it their sender, subject, beginning of text and attachment names.
organization.skipAutomated: Set plainly automated mail aside first (newsletters, notifications)
organization.modelHint: Used by members who have not chosen their own. Leave empty for the server's.
organization.key: OpenRouter API key of the organisation
organization.keyHint: Encrypted in the database. Used by every member who has no key of their own.
organization.automationNone: On demand: the AI writes only when a member asks
organization.automationDraft: Prepared at fetch, to review here
organization.automationMailbox: Prepared at fetch and filed in the mailbox’s Drafts folder
organization.automationHint: Preparing at fetch sends the content of each email to handle to the AI, at most ten per fetch and mailbox. Nothing is ever sent to the correspondent without a member’s confirmation.

welcome.promptIntro: A prompt tells the AI how your organisation replies: its tone, its rules. One is ready. Read it, make it yours, and add others now or later in Prompts.
welcome.workIntro: How much the AI does before you open an email. Whatever you choose, nothing is sent until someone confirms it.
welcome.workLegend: For every member of the organisation
welcome.manualHint: Every email of the watched folder is to handle. The AI writes only when I ask. Nothing is sent to it until then.
welcome.sortHint: The AI sets aside what needs no reply and suggests a prompt. It reads the sender, the subject, the beginning of the text and attachment names.
welcome.draftHint: As above, and a proposal is written at fetch for each email to handle. Their content is sent to the AI without anyone asking.
welcome.mailboxHint: As above, and each proposal is filed in the Drafts folder of the mailbox, to finish and send from my mail client.
welcome.needsKey: Needs an AI key, which was not given.
welcome.workLater: This can be changed at any time in Settings → Organisation.
welcome.finish: Apply and open a first email
welcome.tryIt: This is your first email here. Write a few words on what to answer, or nothing at all, then “Write with”. Nothing is sent until you confirm.
welcome.tryPrepared: This is your first email here, with the proposal prepared for it. Read it, change what you want, then Send. Nothing is sent until you confirm.
